---
title: Carry changes back
description: Notice what people change in Marfa in a connector's items, carry those changes back to the vendor, and create at the vendor what people make in Marfa.
---

The items a connector [pulls](/build/connector-pull) are ordinary items, and people and apps edit, archive and move them to the bin. A two-way connector notices those changes and carries them back to the vendor. The examples follow an online shop connector with a key of its own under the source `shop`, which writes the type `shop.order`.

## With the kit

A connector built on [the connector kit](/build/connector) names `link_field` in its type and adds `onChange`. The kit watches the event stream, keeps the agreements, and calls `onChange` once for each item with a change the vendor hasn't had:

```ts title="src/main.ts"
async onChange({ kind, item, changed }, { env, signal, setLink }) {
  const id = item.properties["order_id"];
  if (typeof id !== "string") {
    const made = await createOrder(env, signal, item);
    await setLink(item, made.id);
    return;
  }
  await updateOrder(env, signal, id, kind, changed, item);
},
```

- **`kind`** is `created`, `updated`, `restored`, `archived`, `trashed` or `purged`, and `changed` names the fields changed in Marfa and not yet carried.
- **`setLink`** writes the vendor's ID onto an item the vendor just made.
- **Throw `Unreachable`** for a failure that can pass, such as a rate limit, and the change is sent again next run. **Throw `Refused`** for a change the vendor will never take, and it isn't sent again until the item changes. **Throw `Declined`** for a change the vendor isn't to be asked about, and the kit puts the fields back.

The [kit's README](https://github.com/withmarfa/marfa-connectors/blob/main/template/README.md#carrying-changes-back) covers `remake`, `preflight` and the rest of the rules.

## On the API

The sections below are the operations underneath, for a connector built directly on the API. In the TypeScript examples, `marfa` is a [TypeScript SDK](/reference/typescript-sdk) client made with the connector's key, `connectorId` is the registration's ID, and `processName` is the name the process took the [hold](/build/connector-holds-and-retries#take-the-hold) under.

### Link items to the vendor

A two-way type names a `link_field` when you [register it](/reference/api/types/registerType): the property that holds the vendor's own ID for the record. Marfa keeps the value unique within the type, in every state, and refuses a second item holding it as `409 link_taken`. An item with no value there is one the vendor hasn't been told about.

### Watch for changes made in Marfa

Follow [the event stream](/reference/api/event-stream/streamEvents) for your type. Each change arrives as an event with the item as it now stands, and `Last-Event-ID` resumes after the last event you handled, so keep that cursor in the state document. [Keep a copy in sync](/build/keep-in-sync) explains the stream.

```http title="Request"
GET /events?type=shop.order
Authorization: Bearer $MARFA_API_KEY
Last-Event-ID: 11
```

Your own writes **come back on the stream too**. To tell a person's change from yours, keep an agreement for each item: what the connector and the vendor last agreed it holds. After every write you make or carry, [write the agreement](/reference/api/connector-state/writeConnectorAgreements) under the hold:

```http tab="HTTP" tab-group="client"
POST /connectors/01a12313-d219-7e92-8869-1f6546b43dbc/agreements
Authorization: Bearer $MARFA_API_KEY
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "process": "8f14e45f-ceea-467a-9c1b-5b3e1c3e0a2d",
  "set": [
    { "item_id": "01a12313-fd4a-78a1-af1e-32792c3df63b", "waiting": false, "record": { "title": "Oil paints", "status": "paid" } }
  ]
}
```

```ts tab="TypeScript"
await marfa.POST("/connectors/{id}/agreements", {
  params: { path: { id: connectorId } },
  body: {
    process: processName,
    set: [
      { item_id: "01a12313-fd4a-78a1-af1e-32792c3df63b", waiting: false, record: { title: "Oil paints", status: "paid" } },
    ],
  },
});
```

When an event arrives, [look up the item's agreement](/reference/api/connector-state/lookupConnectorAgreements) and compare:

- **The item matches the `record`:** the change is one already agreed, such as your own write.
- **The item differs:** someone changed it in Marfa. Write the agreement again with `waiting: true` and the `record` unchanged, so it still says what was agreed and now says a change waits for the vendor.

Record the change **before you move the cursor** past its event. A process that stops between the two then reads the event again and finds the agreement waiting; the other way round, a stop loses the change.

### Carry a change back

[List the agreements](/reference/api/connector-state/listConnectorAgreements) that wait:

```http tab="HTTP" tab-group="client"
GET /connectors/01a12313-d219-7e92-8869-1f6546b43dbc/agreements?waiting=true
Authorization: Bearer $MARFA_API_KEY
```

```ts tab="TypeScript"
const { data } = await marfa.GET("/connectors/{id}/agreements", {
  params: { path: { id: connectorId }, query: { waiting: true } },
});
```

```json title="Response" status="200"
{
  "data": [
    {
      "item_id": "01a12313-fd4a-78a1-af1e-32792c3df63b",
      "waiting": true,
      "record": { "title": "Oil paints", "status": "paid" },
      "updated_at": "2026-11-19T00:23:44.000Z"
    }
  ],
  "next_cursor": null
}
```

For each one, read the item, send the vendor what changed, and once the vendor has taken it, write the agreement with `waiting: false` and a `record` of what both sides now hold.

If the vendor refuses the change or doesn't answer, leave the agreement waiting, say why in the run's report, and try again on the next run. **Never clear** a waiting agreement to move on: the change would be lost.

### Send a new item to the vendor

A person can make an item of your type in Marfa, and a two-way connector creates it at the vendor. For each item with no link:

1. Create the record at the vendor, sending the item's `id` as the vendor's idempotency key if it takes one, so a retry can't create it twice.
2. [Update the item](/reference/api/items/updateItem) to set the link, sending the `version` you read.
3. Write the item's agreement.

```http tab="HTTP" tab-group="client"
PATCH /items/01a12314-5e6a-7687-b04c-d62fa7beeccb
Authorization: Bearer $MARFA_API_KEY
Content-Type: application/json

{ "version": 1, "properties": { "order_id": "4020" } }
```

```ts tab="TypeScript"
await marfa.PATCH("/items/{id}", {
  params: { path: { id: "01a12314-5e6a-7687-b04c-d62fa7beeccb" } },
  body: { version: 1, properties: { order_id: "4020" } },
});
```

Set the link **straight after the vendor answers**. A run that stops between the two sends the create again, and the vendor's idempotency key answers it with the record already made.

### Rare cases

- **A conflict:** a person and the vendor changed the same field, so both differ from the `record`. Marfa doesn't decide which wins: choose a rule and apply it every time. The kit takes the later change, and a vendor that names no time loses.
- **A purge at a vendor that can't delete:** change the record instead, such as by closing the order, then [settle the tombstone](/reference/api/items/settleTombstones) to the time of that change. Otherwise the next pull reads the change and brings the record back as a new item.

The rules behind this page are in the [connectors](https://github.com/withmarfa/marfa/blob/main/conformance/spec/connectors.md#writing-agreements) and [items](https://github.com/withmarfa/marfa/blob/main/conformance/spec/items.md) chapters of the contract.
